question.text: How does the Black (1976) model differ from the Black-Scholes model?

answer.text: Black 1976 uses forward/futures prices instead of spot prices as input
Black 1976 can price American options while Black-Scholes cannot
Black 1976 uses historical volatility while Black-Scholes uses implied volatility
There is no difference — they give the same results

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 78 of the source explains that Black (1976) substitutes the spot price with a discounted future price and is used for valuing options on futures. Page 79 states explicitly that Black uses forward/future prices while Black-Scholes uses spot prices. The Trap: Both models can use the same volatility input; the distinguishing feature is the underlying price (forward/future vs spot), not the volatility type or the American/European exercise style. Note: Page 79 confirms that Indian exchanges use Black 1976 for exchange-traded interest rate options.
